The recommendations of Wall Street analysts are often relied on by investors when deciding whether to buy, sell, or hold a stock. Media reports about these brokerage-firm-employed (or sell-side) analysts changing their ratings often affect a stock's price. Do they really matter, though?

Let's take a look at what these Wall Street heavyweights have to say about MercadoLibre (MELI) before we discuss the reliability of brokerage recommendations and how to use them to your advantage.

MercadoLibre currently has an average brokerage recommendation (ABR) of 1.45, on a scale of 1 to 5 (Strong Buy to Strong Sell), calculated based on the actual recommendations (Buy, Hold, Sell, etc.) made by 19 brokerage firms. An ABR of 1.45 approximates between Strong Buy and Buy.

Of the 19 recommendations that derive the current ABR, 14 are Strong Buy and one is Buy. Strong Buy and Buy respectively account for 73.7% and 5.3% of all recommendations.

Brokerage Recommendation Trends for MELI

Check price target & stock forecast for MercadoLibre here>>>

While the ABR calls for buying MercadoLibre, it may not be wise to make an investment decision solely based on this information. Several studies have shown limited to no success of brokerage recommendations in guiding investors to pick stocks with the best price increase potential.

Are you wondering why? The vested interest of brokerage firms in a stock they cover often results in a strong positive bias of their analysts in rating it. Our research shows that for every "Strong Sell" recommendation, brokerage firms assign five "Strong Buy" recommendations.

This means that the interests of these institutions are not always aligned with those of retail investors, giving little insight into the direction of a stock's future price movement. It would therefore be best to use this information to validate your own analysis or a tool that has proven to be highly effective at predicting stock price movements.

With an impressive externally audited track record, our proprietary stock rating tool, the Zacks Rank, which classifies stocks into five groups, ranging from Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy) to Zacks Rank #5 (Strong Sell), is a reliable indicator of a stock's near-term price performance. So, validating the Zacks Rank with ABR could go a long way in making a profitable investment decision.

Zacks Rank Should Not Be Confused With ABR

In spite of the fact that Zacks Rank and ABR both appear on a scale from 1 to 5, they are two completely different measures.

Broker recommendations are the sole basis for calculating the ABR, which is typically displayed in decimals (such as 1.28). The Zacks Rank, on the other hand, is a quantitative model designed to harness the power of earnings estimate revisions. It is displayed in whole numbers -- 1 to 5.

MercadoLibre recently rolled out one hour delivery in São Paulo and moved into selling prescription medicines in Brazil, while also raising US$1b in long term notes to support logistics and credit operations, alongside quarterly revenue growth paired with weaker operating income and margins.

The combination of faster delivery promises and higher capital spending highlights a trade off between building scale in Brazil and near term pressure on MercadoLibre's profitability profile.

We will now explore how MercadoLibre's investment narrative is affected by this push into one hour delivery and prescription medicine sales.

Compare MercadoLibre's push into faster delivery with a curated set of logistics heavyweights and capital disciplined platforms in our list of solid balance sheet and fundamentals (25 results).

MercadoLibre Investment Narrative Recap

To own MercadoLibre, you need to believe that its heavy reinvestment in logistics, payments and credit eventually supports healthier unit economics rather than leaving margins under pressure. The recent launch of one hour delivery and prescription drug sales in Brazil pushes more volume into an already dense network. The short term swing factor is margin stabilization, since Q2 already showed weaker operating income.

The biggest risk right now sits in the combination of thinner profitability and a growing credit book funded with a high level of debt. Faster shipping and a broader assortment do not change that risk directly, but they can add complexity if higher volumes coincide with softer credit quality or prolonged higher shipping and marketing costs.

The most relevant recent move for this story is the US$1b long term notes issue. That funding is earmarked for logistics and credit growth, which ties directly into one hour delivery promises and the broader MercadoLibre ecosystem. Extra liquidity gives the business more room to keep free shipping thresholds low and expand first party assortment while maintaining its fulfillment build out.

The trade off is that more borrowing adds to an already leveraged balance sheet. For you as a shareholder, the key question is whether incremental returns from denser logistics and a larger US$16.4b credit book offset higher interest expense and the risk of future credit losses. Those outcomes feed straight into the margin path that many investors are watching closely over the next few years.

MercadoLibre's narrative projects US$75.8b revenue and US$5.2b earnings by 2029. This aligns with analysts assuming 29.1% yearly revenue growth and implies earnings need to rise by about US$3.3b from US$1.9b today.

title: Better Retail Stock for 2026: GameStop vs. MercadoLibre

Deciding between GameStop (NYSE:GME) and MercadoLibre (NASDAQ:MELI) requires balancing a traditional retail recovery against a rapidly expanding fintech and e-commerce ecosystem. Which of these two companies is the better buy for your portfolio today?

GameStop and MercadoLibre represent two very different approaches to the retail sector, ranging from a turnaround story in physical gaming to an e-commerce powerhouse in Latin America. Investors often compare them to determine whether value or high growth offers better long-term potential. This comparison breaks down their financial health and risks to help you decide.

The case for GameStop

GameStop operates as a specialty retailer selling games, collectibles, and entertainment products through a global network of stores and digital platforms. As of January 31, 2026, the company managed 2,206 stores across the United States, Europe, and Australia under brands like EB Games and Micromania. Its business relies on strong relationships with major vendors, including Nintendo and Sony, which provide the hardware and software central to its sales strategy.

In its 2025 fiscal year (FY), ended Jan. 31, revenue reached $3.6 billion, representing a decline of 5.1% compared to the prior year. Despite lower sales, the company reported net income of $418.4 million, which is a significant increase from the $131.3 million earned in FY 2024. This improvement in the bottom line reflects a substantial jump in net margin to 11.5% from the 3.4% seen in the previous fiscal year.

As of its January 2026 balance sheet, the debt-to-equity ratio was 0.8x, representing total debt, including short-term obligations, divided by shareholder equity. The current ratio, which measures how well current assets cover liabilities due within one year, reached 15.3x. Free cash flow, calculated as cash flow from operations minus capital expenditures, was $597.3 million for the period.

The case for MercadoLibre

MercadoLibre operates a vast ecosystem across Latin America that includes its marketplace, Mercado Pago for payments, and Mercado Envíos for logistics. The company is a prominent player among retail stocks and serves millions of buyers and sellers across 18 countries. It recently streamlined its offerings by discontinuing the Mercado Shops service at the end of 2025 to focus on its high-growth fintech and core commerce platforms.

In FY 2025, revenue reached $28.9 billion, marking a robust growth rate of 39.1% year over year. The company generated net income of $2.0 billion during this period, up from $1.9 billion in FY 2024. While revenue grew quickly, the net margin decreased slightly to 6.9% compared to the 9.2% reported in the previous fiscal year.

title: MercadoLibre Stock Is Down 13% Over the Past Year. Can 109.7% Upside Change That?

MercadoLibre Stock Is Down 13% Over the Past Year. Can 109.7% Upside Change That?

Key Stats for MELI Stock

Past week performance: -3.1%

52-week range: $1,495 to $2,428

Valuation model target price: $3,846

Implied upside: 109.7% over 2.2 years

MercadoLibre Doubles Down on Speed in Brazil

MercadoLibre (MELI) shares fell about 3.1% over the past week to roughly $1,834, leaving the stock 24% below its 52-week high. The pullback came even after election results lifted Brazil's stock exchange to a record in early October. Investors are not doubting the growth. Instead, they are questioning how long margins stay under pressure.

The latest move is a speed play. MercadoLibre launched deliveries within one hour in São Paulo for items up to 15 kilograms, including food and medications. It also began selling prescription medicines through its own São Paulo pharmacy and targets 20 partner locations by year-end. Timing matters here, since Sea's Shopee launched four-hour delivery in Brazil in August.

Q2 results show the trade-off clearly. Net revenue jumped 50% to $10.2 billion, topping $10 billion for the first time. However, operating income fell 17% to $683 million, and operating margin compressed 5.5 percentage points to 6.7%. Net income dropped 11% to $466 million, marking a third straight quarter of year-over-year declines.

CEO Ariel Szarfsztejn described AI as "accelerating the secular shift we already are trying to capture," pointing to better search and lending decisions. The company also raised $1 billion in 10-year notes at a coupon near 5.9%, which strengthens liquidity for logistics and credit growth. Going forward, MELI stock likely hinges on whether Q3 shows margins stabilizing while growth stays above 40%.

Margins Are the Whole Valuation Debate
MELI Guided Valuation Model (TIKR)

Under valuation model assumptions realized through 12/31/28, the stock is modeled using:

Revenue Growth (CAGR): 32.4%

Operating Margins: 8.3%

Exit P/E Multiple: 40.6x

Based on these inputs, the model estimates a target price of $3,846, implying a 109.7% total return from the current share price of $1,834 and an annualized return of 39.8% over the next 2.2 years.

This is a margin compression story with a recovery bet attached. MercadoLibre's operating margin was 12.7% over the past year in the model, but Q2 slipped to 6.7% as free shipping and credit spending ramped up. The model assumes 8.3%, which equals the trailing margin today. So the forecast needs no full rebound, just no further damage.

MELI Guided Valuation Model (TIKR)

Growth assumptions look conservative against the company's record. Revenue grew 39.1% over the last year and 48.7% annually over five years, while analysts expect about 36.9% over the next two years. The model's 32.4% input therefore leaves a cushion. Mercado Pago's credit book, up 75% to $16.4 billion, keeps feeding that top line.

The 40.6x exit multiple matches the past year's P/E and sits well below the 64.3x five-year average. Today's forward P/E, the price paid for each $1 of next year's expected profit, is near 43.5x. That means the model actually assumes slight compression. A 39.8% annual return is exceptional, but it depends on the investment cycle paying off while Sea Limited (SE) keeps pricing pressure on Brazil.

Shopee Is Chasing MercadoLibre Into Brazil

Sea Limited (SE), owner of Shopee, is MercadoLibre's most aggressive rival in Brazil. Sea's Q2 revenue rose 48.1% to $7.8 billion, nearly matching MercadoLibre's 50% growth. Shopee's gross merchandise volume (GMV), the total value of goods sold, grew 28.4% to $38.3 billion. Sea's management also called Brazil its fastest-growing market in the quarter.

Fintech is a head-to-head race too. Sea's lending arm, Monee, grew revenue 58.9% to $1.4 billion, with loans outstanding up 62.5% to $11.1 billion. Mercado Pago's credit portfolio is larger at $16.4 billion and growing faster at 75%. That lead gives MercadoLibre more data to price risk, which supports credit margins.

Profitability shows where the money goes. Shopee earned $255.4 million in adjusted EBITDA on $5.6 billion of revenue, a margin of roughly 4.6%. Although the measures differ, MercadoLibre's 6.7% operating margin remains higher even after this year's spending. Amazon (AMZN) also competes in Brazil and Mexico, yet MercadoLibre's moat is its owned logistics network, which delivered 77% of fast shipments in Brazil within 48 hours.

*__Weigh the projected EBIT turnaround against three straight quarters of profit declines >>>__*

What's Driving MELI Stock Going Forward?

Q3 results on November 2 come first. Investors want to see whether operating margin holds near Q2's 6.7% or slips again. The Q2 shareholder letter described the squeeze as a deliberate choice to reinvest efficiency gains into the customer offer. So any commentary on shipping subsidies will matter as much as revenue.

Brazil's quick commerce push is the near-term swing factor. One-hour delivery and pharmacy sales increase how often customers open the app, which lifts order frequency and advertising value. These services also require more fulfillment centers and couriers, so costs arrive before revenue. Past cuts to seller shipping fees in 2024 and 2025 followed the same pattern and strengthened engagement.

Credit remains the profit engine. Net interest margin after losses, a measure of lending profit after bad loans, improved from 18% in Q1 to 21% in Q2. Mercado Pago is also expanding its credit card business despite concerns about Brazilian consumer debt. Fresh bond funding gives MercadoLibre room to keep growing that book through 2027.

MercadoLibre's Expanding Ecosystem Supports Growth

MercadoLibre continues to benefit from the increasing adoption of e-commerce and digital financial services across Latin America. Its integrated ecosystem, encompassing Commerce, fintech, logistics and advertising, strengthens customer engagement while creating opportunities for sustainable growth. In second-quarter 2026, net revenues and financial income increased 50% year over year to $10.2 billion, reflecting strong momentum across its operations.

The company's Commerce business benefits from its expanding product assortment, improving delivery capabilities and initiatives focused on affordability and convenience. Lower free-shipping thresholds in Brazil have encouraged more frequent purchases and stronger customer retention. Meanwhile, investments in first-party offerings and cross-border trade are broadening product availability and supporting marketplace activity. Its established logistics network enhances delivery efficiency and reinforces its competitive positioning.

Mercado Pago remains a key growth catalyst, supported by rising adoption of digital payments, credit cards and other financial services. The company's ability to leverage its commerce ecosystem and transaction data supports credit underwriting and personalized financial offerings. Expanding credit-card adoption also encourages deeper customer engagement across both platforms, strengthening cross-selling opportunities.

Advertising provides another avenue for growth, with Mercado Ads benefiting from increasing merchant participation and improved monetization capabilities. AI-powered advertising tools are helping sellers optimize campaigns, while enhanced marketplace search capabilities are supporting customer conversion and engagement.

The growing number of customers using both Commerce and Mercado Pago further strengthens MercadoLibre's competitive advantage. This interconnected business model encourages higher transaction frequency, customer loyalty and greater use of financial services, providing a solid foundation for long-term growth.

Reflecting On Online Marketplace Stocks' Q2 Earnings: MercadoLibre (NASDAQ:MELI)

As the Q2 earnings season comes to a close, it's time to take stock of this quarter's best and worst performers in the online marketplace industry, including MercadoLibre (NASDAQ:MELI) and its peers.

Marketplaces have existed for centuries. Where once it was a main street in a small town or a mall in the suburbs, sellers benefitted from proximity to one another because they could draw customers by offering convenience and selection. Today, a myriad of online marketplaces fulfill that same role, aggregating large customer bases, which attracts commission-paying sellers, generating flywheel scale effects that feed back into further customer acquisition.

The 11 online marketplace stocks we track reported a satisfactory Q2. As a group, revenues beat analysts' consensus estimates by 1.9% while next quarter's revenue guidance was 1.8% below.

Amidst this news, share prices of the companies have had a rough stretch. On average, they are down 9.6% since the latest earnings results.

MercadoLibre (NASDAQ:MELI)

Originally started as an online auction platform, MercadoLibre (NASDAQ:MELI) is a one-stop e-commerce marketplace and fintech platform in Latin America.

MercadoLibre reported revenues of $10.17 billion, up 49.8% year on year. This print exceeded analysts' expectations by 4.5%. Overall, it was an exceptional quarter for the company with a solid beat of analysts' EBITDA estimates and impressive growth in its users.

MercadoLibre Total Revenue

MercadoLibre scored the fastest revenue growth in the group. The company reported 89 million daily active users, up 25.4% year on year. Investor expectations, however, were likely higher than Wall Street's published projections, leaving some wishing for even better results (analysts' consensus estimates are those published by big banks and advisory firms, not the investors who make buy and sell decisions). What Happened?

MercadoLibre (MELI:NASDAQ) closed at $1,892.44 on October 12, 2026. That is 9.5% above its September 30 close, a gain that followed a rally in Brazilian assets set off by Brazil's first-round presidential vote. Brazil supplied 52.6% of the company's 2025 revenue, so the stock moved with the country.

Whether to sell into that gain or add to it depends less on the October 25 runoff than on the margin and credit trends management laid out in its Q2 2026 investor relations materials.

A Re-Rating, Not an Upgrade

Flávio Bolsonaro took 47.03% of valid votes to Lula's 45.16% on October 4. The next day, the Ibovespa closed at a record 206,912, up 7.7%, with Brazilian banks leading the rally. MercadoLibre was a secondary beneficiary, trading nearly 8% higher in the October 5 morning session. A Datafolha poll on October 8 showed Bolsonaro ahead 49% to 45%, still a technical tie.

The gain came from the multiple. MercadoLibre's NTM P/E ratio rose from about 41x on September 30 to about 45x on October 12, while consensus NTM EPS held at around $42. Investors are paying more for the same forecast.

The Street is less enthusiastic than the stock price. Between September 30 and October 12, hold ratings rose to six from four out of 26 analysts; the full split is 16 Buy, 4 Outperform, and 6 Hold. The mean target of around $2,270 sits about 20% above the current price.

MercadoLibre NTM Price / Normalized Earnings (P/E) (TIKR)
Lower Rates Would Help, but Only a Little

Lower Brazilian policy rates were already on analysts' minds before the vote; HSBC's Neha Agarwala asked about them on the Q2 call. In reply, Osvaldo Giménez, President of Fintech, said credit and acquiring prices reset with policy rates, so the benefit there is marginal.

The Marketplace gains slightly more, because the company does not reprice its interest-free installment plans as often. CFO Martin de los Santos added: "The Marketplace, typically, when interest rates come down, we improve a little bit margins."

A little is the right size. The Q2 EBIT margin was 6.72%, down from 12.15% a year earlier. The company attributes the decline to deliberate investment, including lower seller take rates in Brazil and higher device costs in acquiring. Rates alone will not close that gap.

Credit is the bigger swing factor. Giménez said that "so far, we are not seeing any deceleration or deterioration of credit book in Brazil." Non-performing loans 15 to 90 days past due sat at 7.0% for the portfolio and 4.6% for credit cards, both near historical lows. The caveat is that loans more than 90 days past due rose in Q2. Management tied that to one product whose early borrowers defaulted above expectations before issuance slowed.

MercadoLibre (NASDAQ:MELI) posted a quarter that looks like two different companies stapled together. In its fiscal second quarter of 2026, net revenue and financial income jumped 50% to $10,169 million. Income from operations fell 17% to $683 million. Management described the profit squeeze as a deliberate choice to plow operating leverage back into its value proposition.

MercadoLibre is the region's best-known online marketplace, plus a lot more. It earns commissions and shipping fees on goods sold, sells ads to merchants, and runs Mercado Pago, a fintech arm that processes payments, holds deposits, and lends money. Brazil, Mexico, and Argentina are its biggest markets.

So the real question is whether investors are watching a company invest in a wider moat, or one that has to pay more just to keep growing. The answer depends on what that spending is actually buying, a dynamic long-term investors weigh when eyeing transformative secular plays like the 10 Stocks That Will Change the World by 2030.

MercadoLibre (MELI) Trades Profit for Scale. Smart Bet or Warning?
An Ecosystem That Feeds Itself

MercadoLibre's edge isn't any single business. It's how the pieces push customers into one another. Shoppers who pay with Mercado Pago become borrowers, borrowers come back to shop, and sellers follow the traffic. The user numbers show that loop working. Unique active buyers reached 89 million in the second quarter, up from 71 million a year earlier. Fintech monthly active users climbed to 88 million from 68 million.

Advertising is the newest layer. Ad revenue grew 62% on an FX-neutral basis (stripping out currency swings), and the company says Mercado Ads topped a 10% share of Latin America's digital ad market for the first time. Selling space to merchants who already depend on the platform is the same retail-media logic behind Amazon's advertising business.

Cheaper Shipping, More Orders

The biggest bet is in Brazil. MercadoLibre lowered its free-shipping threshold there last year, and the payoff is visible in volume. Brazilian items sold rose 56% year over year in the second quarter, while gross merchandise volume (the total value of goods sold) grew 39% FX-neutral.

Company-wide, items sold hit 795 million, up from 550 million. The catch is cost. Higher shipping expenses weren't fully offset by revenue, which squeezed gross margin. Still, the company says free and slow shipments are now contribution-positive across half of the R$19 to R$79 price range, a sign the cheaper orders are starting to pay their own way.

Lending is the other engine. The credit portfolio passed $16 billion, up 75%, and 2.6 million new credit cards went out during the quarter. That push puts it alongside 10 Most Promising Fintech Stocks to Buy Now. NIMAL (net interest margin after losses) slipped to 20.7% from 23.0% a year ago, but improved 3 percentage points from the prior quarter.
